Control-channel jitter, not video arrival jitter. A session value, not a window value; reported only after 8 RTT samples (one per receiver ping, about every 2 s).

Control-message round trip; it rides behind any queued video on the same connection. Both ends of the span are this device's wall clock (the ping time also feeds the clock offset), so a clock step during a round trip skews one sample; samples outside 0-2000 ms are dropped.
Cost of a capture restart: the operator changes the frame-rate cap mid-trial and back.
Counts duplicates and replays too; see the submit counters for source-unique frames.
Counts extractions, not frames. Never per frame; the Colour metadata group reports what they found.
Counts only commands yielded while diagnostics were on.
Cross-device spans use a ping/pong clock offset; error is up to about half the best round trip.

Display capture only (Mirror, Extend). The closest available proxy for source-unique frames: ScreenCaptureKit sends a complete frame when content changed.

Duplicates by design (heal a lost frame).

Experimental Metal path only, which itself changes timing. Starts at encoder submission, not capture. Not capture-to-photon. Values outside -50 to 5000 ms are dropped, so p99 and max under-report a pathological latency.
Experimental Metal path only. The only presentation this app can observe.
Experimental Metal path only; only while the lab fixture is visible.
Fixture restarted; counting starts again from the new ID.

Includes VideoToolbox's own queueing when more than one frame is in flight (StreamingPriority in-flight limit 1/2/3).
Includes the rate limiter's trailing-edge hold and any replay delay. Display capture only: Window view composites have no capture PTS, so nothing is recorded there.
Keep hands off both devices while the trial measures.

One sample per restart (resync, reconnect). The arrival interval restarts its baseline at a restart, so this gap is not in it.
Only the experimental Metal path reports an observed presentation, and it changes timing itself.

Smoothed absolute difference of successive RTT samples (RFC 3550: starts at 0, gain 1/16), over the session
Source-unique fixture frames that reached the decoded-frame handoff.

Start Window View and add only the fixture window as a pane; maximise that pane on the receiver.

StreamReceiver.presentDecodedSample: successive complete video frames off the wire
Submission repeating the previous submission's capture PTS
Submission whose capture PTS differs from the previous submission's

The default AVSampleBufferDisplayLayer path decodes inside the system layer and reports no decode time.
The encoder already had its in-flight limit of frames.
The engine composes only when a pane changed, plus about one resend per second when static.
The performance overlay labels this "encode". cap is stamped at encoder submission, not at capture, so this is encode plus packaging, not capture-to-send.

The performance overlay labels this "latency". It starts at encoder submission (not capture) and ends when the frame is handed to the presenter, before any A/V delay, queueing, decode or display. Offset error is up to about half the best round trip. Values outside -50 to 5000 ms are dropped (clock mapping not settled), so p99 and max under-report a pathological latency.
The same source frame handed over again (replay, static resend or re-encode).
The source did not change; not a drop.
The trailing-edge hold released the last change on screen.
The transport still had its limit of unsent video frames.
Trials cover whole 5 s diagnostics windows after the warm-up; up to one window at each end is outside the measurement.
Turn on Streaming Diagnostics on this Mac and on the receiving device (iPhone/iPad: Settings > Diagnostics > Streaming Diagnostics).

Uniqueness comes from the compose counters, not the PTS.
VTCompressionSession submit (MacSender.encode) to its output callback

Video payload only; framing, TLS, QUIC/TCP and IP overhead are not counted.

What a still screen costs: should be close to no new frames, only the periodic resend.
Whole process, sampled once per window (5 s). Not GPU, encoder or decoder hardware load.
